title: verifier.code context
description: The context object of a `code` request. SPEC.md section 3.1: the top-level request schema constrains `context` only to `type: object`; each profile closes its own shape here. Nothing in this object is tied to either caller — the same shape serves Portage's fail-up guard and, later, Cairn's grading runner.

working_dir.description: Directory the commands run in. Relative paths resolve against the verifier's own working directory, which is how a golden case stays machine-independent (SPEC.md section 8: absolute paths that differ per machine are a determinism hazard).

commands.description: The command set. Every key is optional: an absent command is a check that was not configured, which is not the same as a check that passed, and the verdict's evidence records which of the two it was.

argv.description: An argv vector, never a shell string. A shell string would make the verdict depend on the shell, and a verifier's decision must depend on nothing but the request (SPEC.md section 8).
